```{python}
    "font.size": 12,
})
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
```

## 4 · The stack {.smaller}

[The Python viz stack]{.eyebrow}

### One grammar, four altitudes

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Most genomics figures are built by [layering]{.down} tools, not switching
between them. `matplotlib` is the canvas; [seaborn]{.down} gives statistical
defaults; [plotly]{.alt} makes it interactive for the browser.

Pick the [lowest layer that still feels effortless]{.up} — drop down only
when you need pixel control.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.keybox}
[Layer 04 · interaction]{.keylabel}
**plotly · bokeh** — hover, zoom, link → ship to the browser
:::
::: {.card}
**Layer 03 · seaborn** — tidy data → statistical defaults<br>
**Layer 02 · matplotlib** — figures, axes, artists (the canvas)<br>
**Layer 01 · pandas / numpy / anndata** — the frame everything is drawn from
:::

## 5 · Volcano {.smaller}

[Differential expression]{.eyebrow}

### Volcano plots in three artists

Map effect size to `x` and significance to `y`, then spend color on direction:
[up-regulated]{.up}, [down-regulated]{.down}, everything else stays quiet grey.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Code · matplotlib

```{python}
#| label: volcano-code
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "4-6"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# direction + significance → color
sig = (df.padj < 0.05) & (df.log2fc.abs() > 1)
col = np.where(df.log2fc >  1, "#c0473a",
       np.where(df.log2fc < -1, "#208462", "#b9b4a7"))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4.5))
ax.scatter(df.log2fc, -np.log10(df.padj),
           c=col, s=14, alpha=.7, edgecolor="none")
ax.axhline(-np.log10(.05), ls="--", lw=.8, color="#8a8578")
ax.axvline( 1, ls="--", lw=.8); ax.axvline(-1, ls="--", lw=.8)
ax.set_xlabel("log$_2$ fold-change"); ax.set_ylabel("-log$_{10}$ adj. p")
```

### Plot

```{python}
#| label: volcano-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.6
x = rng.normal(0, 2.1, 900)
y = np.abs(x) * 1.1 + rng.gamma(1.1, 1.0, 900) * (np.abs(x) > 1)
y = np.clip(y + rng.normal(0, .4, 900), 0, 12)
col = np.where((x > 1) & (y > 1.3), RED,
       np.where((x < -1) & (y > 1.3), GREEN, GREY))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.6))
ax.scatter(x, y, c=col, s=16, alpha=.7, edgecolor="none")
ax.axhline(1.3, ls="--", lw=.8, color="#8a8578")
ax.axvline( 1, ls="--", lw=.8, color="#c9c3b3")
ax.axvline(-1, ls="--", lw=.8, color="#c9c3b3")
ax.set_xlabel("log$_2$ fold-change"); ax.set_ylabel("-log$_{10}$ adj. p")
plt.show()
```

:::


## 6 · Heatmap {.smaller}

[Expression heatmaps]{.eyebrow}

### Build it in three moves

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 1 · Base grid

```{python}
#| eval: false
import seaborn as sns
sns.heatmap(expr, cmap="mako", cbar=False)
```

### 2 · + Cluster

```{python}
#| eval: false
sns.clustermap(expr, cmap="mako",
               method="ward", metric="euclidean")
```

### 3 · + Annotate

```{python}
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "3-5"
sns.clustermap(
    expr, cmap="mako",
    col_colors=group_colors,    # condition strip on top
    row_cluster=True, col_cluster=True,
    cbar_pos=(.02, .8, .03, .15),
)
```

:::


## 7 · Takeaway {.center}

> Color is a [variable]{.down}. Spend it on the thing that carries the
> story — never on decoration.

[— a rule we return to every session]{.eyebrow}


## 8 · Manhattan {background-color="#f6f4ee"}

[Genome-wide association]{.eyebrow} · **Manhattan plot · 22 autosomes**

```{python}
#| label: manhattan
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.8
sizes = rng.integers(40, 120, 22)
xs, cs, chrom_mid, off = [], [], [], 0
for i, n in enumerate(sizes):
    pos = off + np.sort(rng.uniform(0, n, n))
    p = -np.log10(rng.uniform(1e-9 if i in (1, 6, 9) else 1e-4, 1, n))
    xs.append(pos); cs.append(np.full(n, GREEN if i % 2 else "#a9b0a2"))
    chrom_mid.append(off + n / 2); off += n
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 4.8))
for pos, p, c, i in zip(xs, [-np.log10(rng.uniform(1e-9 if k in (1,6,9) else 1e-4,1,len(pos))) for k,pos in enumerate(xs)], cs, range(22)):
    ax.scatter(pos, p, c=c, s=7, alpha=.7, edgecolor="none")
ax.axhline(-np.log10(5e-8), ls="--", lw=1.2, color=RED)
ax.set_xticks(chrom_mid); ax.set_xticklabels(range(1, 23), fontsize=8)
ax.set_ylabel("-log$_{10}$(p)"); ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.set_xlim(0, off)
plt.show()
```

### UMAP explorer

::: {.browser}
::: {.bbar}
localhost:8050 / **umap-explorer** · running
:::
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
cents = [(-4,2),(0,-3),(4,1),(5,-3),(-5,-3)]
labels = ["T-cell","Myeloid","B-cell","NK","DC"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9,4))
for (cx,cy),lab in zip(cents, labels):
    pts = rng.normal([cx,cy], .9, (110,2))
    ax.scatter(pts[:,0], pts[:,1], s=14, alpha=.55, color=GREEN, edgecolor="none")
    ax.text(cx, cy+1.6, lab, ha="center", fontsize=9, family="monospace")
ax.set_xlabel("UMAP-1"); ax.set_ylabel("UMAP-2")
ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
plt.show()
```
:::

> In the live session this is a Dash app — sliders for `n_neighbors` / `min_dist`,
> toggles to color by cell type, cluster, or sample.
